body:
## Pull request overview

This PR enhances the ViewConfigPanel component to provide a responsive, accessible inline view configuration experience similar to Airtable. The changes improve mobile UX by implementing a full-screen overlay on small screens while maintaining the existing inline sidebar on desktop, add proper ARIA accessibility attributes, and automatically close the panel when users switch between views.

**Changes:**
- Enhanced ViewConfigPanel with responsive CSS classes (absolute full-width overlay on mobile, relative sidebar on desktop)
- Added ARIA accessibility attributes (role="complementary", aria-label, tabIndex) and focus management
- Implemented auto-close behavior when switching views in ObjectView
- Added workaround comment for CRM example Zod double-parse bug
- Updated ROADMAP documentation to reflect Phase 20 completion

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 6 out of 6 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments.

<details>
<summary>Show a summary per file</summary>

| File | Description |
| ---- | ----------- |
| apps/console/src/components/ViewConfigPanel.tsx | Added responsive positioning (absolute → relative breakpoint), ARIA attributes (role, aria-label, tabIndex), and focus management via useRef + useEffect |
| apps/console/src/components/ObjectView.tsx | Added auto-close logic for ViewConfigPanel when handleViewChange is called (line 127) |
| apps/console/src/__tests__/ViewConfigPanel.test.tsx | Added 2 new tests verifying ARIA attributes and responsive CSS classes (29 total tests now) |
| examples/crm/objectstack.config.ts | Added `{ strict: false }` option with explanatory comment about Zod double-parse bug workaround |
| ROADMAP_CONSOLE.md | Updated Phase 20 description with new features (responsive overlay, ARIA, auto-close) and added v2.1.0 milestone |
| ROADMAP.md | Updated Inline View Config Panel feature description with new capabilities |
</details>

The focus management effect in useEffect is not covered by tests. Consider adding a test to verify that the panel receives focus when opened, which is important for keyboard navigation and accessibility. This can be done by checking if panelRef.current.focus() was called or by verifying focus programmatically in the test.

The auto-close behavior when switching views is not covered by tests. Consider adding a test in ViewSwitching.test.tsx or ObjectView.test.tsx to verify that showViewConfigPanel is set to false when handleViewChange is called. This ensures the panel closes automatically when users switch between views, which is an important UX behavior mentioned in the PR description.
